items.title: Campbell, Laplace, Mecke, and Cox moment formulas
items.statement:
Let $\eta$ be a Poisson point process on the locally compact, second-countable Hausdorff space $S$, with locally finite, sigma-finite intensity measure $
u$. For every nonnegative Borel $f$, its Campbell and Laplace formulas are $\mathbb E[\eta(f)]=
u(f)$ and $\mathbb E[e^{-\eta(f)}]=e^{-
u(1-e^{-f})}$, with $e^{-\infty}=0$. For every nonnegative $g$ measurable for the product of the Borel and evaluation sigma-algebras on $S	imes\mathcal N_{\mathrm{lf}}(S)$, the add-one Mecke formula and its deletion form are $\mathbb E[\int g(x,\eta)\,\eta(dx)]=\int\mathbb E[g(x,\eta+\delta_x)]\,
u(dx)$ and $\mathbb E[\int g(x,\eta-\delta_x)\,\eta(dx)]=\int\mathbb E[g(x,\eta)]\,
u(dx)$; in the second integral one occurrence is deleted at each counted point, with multiplicity retained. Conversely, a locally finite point process with locally finite, sigma-finite mean measure $
u$ is Poisson if it satisfies the deletion identity for every such $g$.
items.strategy: Prove Laplace by simple approximation, extend finite Mecke over independent restrictions, derive the converse from count recurrences, and integrate conditional Poisson moments through the supplied kernel.
